args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: After v2.3.1 was deployed to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api began failing health checks with an 18% error rate. (v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.) The plan was to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy production release, but the rollback was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). checkout-api was instead rolled back in all regions to v2.2.9, the next most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in us-east, us-west and eu-west with a 0.2% error rate. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure; confirm v2.2.9 is not affected by CVE-2026-4417; check whether any features or changes from v2.3.x were lost by going back to v2.2.9.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back in all regions, but to v2.2.9 rather than v2.3.0. The service is healthy again, and the SEV2 incident is open.

1. **Cause:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed in staging.
2. **Rollback:** The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0, but the system rejected that rollback because v2.3.0 is quarantined for a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417). I rolled back to the next most recent healthy release, v2.2.9. It's now running in all three regions, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the blocked rollback to v2.3.0, the rollback to v2.2.9 and the follow-ups below.

**Follow-ups to check:**
- I don't know whether v2.2.9 is also affected by that security vulnerability. Someone should confirm this.
- Going back to v2.2.9 removes everything added in v2.3.0 as well as v2.3.1. Check that nothing depends on those changes.
- The cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs to be found.
